story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: You were talking about this new innovation that's come into the recording business and that's changed the future of music. Where we used to have to go from disc to tape and from tape to sweetening, from sweetening to overdub. You mentioned this new thing, what's that new thing you mentioned?

Digital recording. You know, I had high hopes, when they started like the young rock groups would plan a rhythm section, it was planned, and then they just recorded the track, the Fender bass, then the drums and the guitar and the piano. I was kind of hoping something good would come

of that at one time. I guess it would make for a good, clean recording. That's all it did do, make for a good, clean recording. And the engineers, as Toscannini would say, they wouldn't be Beethoven or Bach, it would be all engineer, which leaves us completely out of it.
Well, they've got what they call good separation.
